reasoning_chain_model: The image shows a Millikan oil-drop experiment setup with parallel plates connected to a voltage source U, oil droplets between the plates, a microscope for observation, and a spray nozzle for creating oil droplets. In Millikan's experiment, he measured the elementary electric charge, specifically the charge of the electron. The experiment worked by balancing gravitational force and electric force on tiny charged oil droplets suspended between capacitor plates. When an electric field is applied, the electric force (qE) balances the gravitational force (mg) when the droplet is suspended, giving the relationship q = mgE/d, where d is the distance between plates. By measuring the mass of droplets, the electric field strength, and analyzing multiple droplets, Millikan was able to determine the fundamental unit of electric charge. Through statistical analysis of many oil droplets, he found that the charge on each droplet was always a multiple of a fundamental value, which became known as the elementary charge or the charge of the electron. Final answer: charge of electron/elementary electric charge.
